title: Modi Begins Two-Day Gujarat Visit, Launches Projects Worth Rs 14,000 Crore
excerpt: In Banaskantha and Ekta Nagar on October 30-31, Modi will dedicate a bovine breeding centre, release Rs 19,000 crore in PM-KISAN aid, launch metro extensions and lead Ekta Diwas celebrations.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi begins a two-day Gujarat visit on October 30, inaugurating and laying foundation stones for projects worth more than Rs 14,000 crore in Banaskantha and over Rs 400 crore in Ekta Nagar.
  • He will release the 24th PM-KISAN instalment of about Rs 19,000 crore for more than nine crore farmer families and flag off two train services.
  • The Banaskantha programme centres on the 127-acre Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre, Ahmedabad Metro extensions to the airport and GIFT City, and widening Ahmedabad-Mehsana Road at about Rs 2,600 crore.
  • The visit ends October 31 with Rashtriya Ekta Diwas at Ekta Nagar, marking Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's 151st birth anniversary.

A two-day programme in Banaskantha and Ekta Nagar

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will begin a two-day visit to Gujarat on October 30, with development programmes in Banaskantha followed by events in Ekta Nagar, Kevadia, ahead of National Unity Day on October 31, according to the Prime Minister's Office release reported by ANI via Indian Economic Observer and The Hindu BusinessLine.

On Friday morning he will visit the Embryo Transfer Technology-In Vitro Fertilisation (ET-IVF) Laboratory and the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre (BBBRC) cattle farm in Banaskantha. He will then lay foundation stones, inaugurate and dedicate projects worth more than Rs 14,000 crore in the district, release the PM-KISAN instalment, flag off two trains and address a public gathering.

Dairy, breeding and farm infrastructure

The BBBRC at Bhildi, spread over 127 acres, will be dedicated to the nation as a Centre of Excellence for bovine breeding, genetic improvement and advanced reproductive technologies. The PMO said it will accelerate breed improvement by 10 to 20 times and is the country's first facility of its kind dedicated to the Kankrej cattle breed.

Modi will also lay foundation stones for two Banas Dairy Bio-CNG plants at Tharad and Radhanpur, processing 75 and 100 metric tonnes of cattle dung per day respectively, dedicate 521 Agriculture Infrastructure Fund projects costing about Rs 4,950 crore, inaugurate the expansion of a potato processing plant at Sanadar, and commission an automated storage system for UHT products at Palanpur. The PM-KISAN release — the 24th instalment, about Rs 19,000 crore — provides direct income support to eligible farmer families across the country.

"More milk per animal, better quality breeds and higher incomes"

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister, on the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre

Metro, roads and Anganwadis

The infrastructure list extends beyond Banaskantha. Modi will lay the foundation stone for Ahmedabad Metro Phase-2A, the airport extension of over 6 km with five stations from Koteshwar Road, and Phase-2B, the GIFT City extension of over 3.3 km with three stations to Shahpur. He will also launch the widening of Ahmedabad-Mehsana Road (State Highway-41) from four lanes to eight lanes at about Rs 2,600 crore, lay the foundation for 4,030 new child-friendly Anganwadi Centres and inaugurate 361 completed centres, an Rs 800 crore initiative the PMO said will benefit more than 4 lakh people.

The two train services are the Ahmedabad (Sabarmati)-Varanasi Express and the Mehsana-Becharaji-Sabarmati MEMU.

Bharat Parv and Ekta Diwas

Later on October 30, Modi will travel to Ekta Nagar to inaugurate Bharat Parv 2026, witness Ekta Prakash Parv and attend the Narmada Aarti. Bharat Parv, running until November 15, is presented as a showcase of states' and Union Territories' traditions, folk performances, cuisines, handicrafts and tourism under the theme of Ek Bharat Shreshth Bharat.

On October 31 he will offer floral tributes at the 182-metre Statue of Unity, inaugurate and lay foundation stones for projects worth over Rs 400 crore in Ekta Nagar — including water and sewage treatment, facade lighting, Narmada Ghat upgrading and tourism projects — and take part in Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations for Patel's 151st birth anniversary, including the Ekta Parade by central and state police forces.

For Gujarati diaspora families, the concrete items to track are the metro airport link, the GIFT City extension and the eight-laning of the Ahmedabad-Mehsana road, which affect travel between Ahmedabad airport, GIFT City and north Gujarat hometowns.
